metadata.Description: My wife and I have had the privilege of watching the sunrise at Honoli'i Beach Park nearly every morning. It has become one of my favorite places on earth. Each sunrise is a breathtaking spectacle, and the park’s landscape provides the perfect backdrop spend your time when starting the day.

metadata.Location: Honoli'I Beach Park, South Hilo, Island of Hawai'i
metadata.Description: This piece captures Honoli'i Beach Park, much like the first, but this time with surfers gracefully riding the waves. Every visit we've made, there have been people out there, embracing the rhythm of the ocean. Their presence enhances the park's tranquil atmosphere, adding a sense of connection between nature and those fortunate enough to experience it. I've often found myself envious of those surfers at dawn, gazing toward the horizon, as it seems to embody the perfect way to greet each new day.

metadata.Description: I've visited Key West numerous times over the past few years, each trip filled with cherished memories shared with family and friends at various spots across the island. This photograph brings me back to those peaceful evenings, watching the sunset with my loved ones, a moment of quiet togetherness against the vibrant hues of the sky.

metadata.Name: Quiet Hour
metadata.Description: I discovered this quiet spot a bit removed from the bustling heart of Mallory Square in Key West, where the atmosphere was much more serene. I especially love the little lizard darting out from beneath the bench in the bottom left corner—it adds a touch of life to the scene. This image has become one of my personal favorites in the collection.

The peaceful moment stood in perfect contrast to the busy day ahead.

metadata.Description: The timing of the catamaran crossing the frame during the sunset was nothing short of perfect. One of my favorite memories from a trip to Key West was when we rented a pontoon boat and ventured out to a sandbar off the island. As we returned, with the sun setting in the distance, I witnessed what may have been the most stunning sunset I've ever seen—its beauty still lingers in my mind.

metadata.Description: This photo was taken near the Halona Blowhole lookout along the Kalaniana'ole Highway on Oahu. A woman in a flowing bright green dress was in the midst of a photoshoot, capturing the attention of passersby. As people climbed down to the beach for a closer look, curiosity sparked about the nature of the shoot. While I never learned what the photoshoot was for, it was fascinating to watch unfold amidst the natural beauty of the scene.

metadata.Name: The Ocean Bellows
metadata.Description: This photo captures the view from the Makapu'u Lighthouse Lookout, looking toward Bellows Beach Field on Oahu. Bellows holds a special place in my heart; I had the privilege of working there early in the summer, and the sight of the beach with the mountains rising in the distance was absolutely breathtaking. I spent nearly three weeks at Bellows in August, and I’m already looking forward to returning in 2025. It’s a place that continues to inspire awe and a deep sense of connection.

metadata.Name: Above the Clouds
metadata.Description: TMy wife and I rented a Jeep Wrangler specifically for the journey to the summit of Mauna Kea on the Big Island to witness the sunset. We’re already planning to stargaze there on our next trip, as we left too early during our last visit. One of my coworkers shared photos of the night sky from the summit, and we've regretted not staying to witness the stars in their full glory.

metadata.Title: Moments by EP
metadata.Info: Memories is a fragment of life forever fixed in the immutable fabric of Bitcoin. This generative artwork depicts a camera, a symbol of the photographic act as a witness to time, but here the lens is not just a visual element, it is a frame where photographs come to life using recursion; synchronized photographs exchange together at the  BTC block height .  These are personal memories, engraved on a Palindrome/Vintage sat, a detail that reinforces the link between the past and the future, between the moment of the shot and its absolute permanence on-chain.  This is not just a visual work, but a statement: what is personal can become eternal, what is ephemeral can defy time. In a world where digital is often synonymous with volatility, this camera frames a memory and makes it indelible. Forever on-chain, forever on Bitcoin.

metadata.Title: Anemone
metadata.Description: "Anemone" is an algorithmic animation that continuously generates ephemeral floral forms. Traces of moving particles weave intricate, flower-like structures, each with a pronounced center. Much like real anemone flowers, these blooms exist briefly before dissolving, only to be reborn in fresh compositions. Each cycle reveals a unique floral shape, ranging from 4 to 9 "petals."  The system undergoes a gradual transformation as particles merge and expand. This interplay between organic behavior is juxtaposed with graphics reminiscent of a hexagonal grid, infusing the piece with a touch of technical aesthetics.

metadata.Title: Mycelioid
metadata.Description: “Mycelioid” captures the intricate patterns that echo the growth of mycelium. These formations evoke cosmic wanderings among celestial bodies or the delicate interactions of the atomic scale. It’s a fusion of macro and microcosmos, where familiar structures emerge, blurring the boundaries between the vast and the minuscule.

metadata.Title: Mycelioid RGB
metadata.Description: “Mycelioid RGB” begins the art diary on blockchain. The “Mycelioid” particle system algorithm will be used as the basis for monthly exploration and development.  For the following months, I will explore artistic process and develop the algorithm. I want to see how the artwork will grow with new features, outputs, and technical solutions. Whether they come from my own explorations, Ordinals protocol or Gamma developing Prints.  The first revision introduces more complex technical solutions: R/G/B channel separation, resulting in a generative color palette and multi-layered WebGL shaders.

metadata.Title: Mycelioid CA
metadata.Description: “Mycelioid CA” is the 3rd entry in the art journal on blockchain. The “CA” stands for Chromatic Aberration — an optical lens quality resulting in chromatic fringing.  The code-simulated light diffraction is fully interactive. Click/tap and drag to adjust the center, strength, and direction of the effect. Hint: explore it on desktop screens and drag beyond the artwork borders.  “Mycelioid CA” is bound up with Bitcoin blockchain by recursive fetch of /blockheight data. With every new block mined on Bitcoin, the initial configuration will change and result in new output.

metadata.Title: Mycelioid DIY
metadata.Description: “Mycelioid DIY” is the 4th entry in the art journal on blockchain. I use the “Mycelioid” particle system algorithm as the basis for monthly exploration and development.  The “DIY” is a whimsical reference for the feature that was introduced in this iteration — the opportunity to manipulate the artwork interactively.  The system’s behavior can be changed by manually adding or removing obstacles: — [left click] / [tap and drag] to add the obstacle — [right click] / [2 finger tap] to reveal all obstacles — [double click] / [3 finger tap] to remove all obstacles  “Mycelioid DIY” is also bond to blockchain by recursive fetch of /blockheight data. Each block mined on Bitcoin alters the initial setup and generates new output.  This time, there’s an extra feature that allows you to input your own seed or blockheight manually: — press [S] on keyboard to open the input window.

metadata.Description: “Mycelioid DOS” is the 5th entry in the art journal on blockchain. I use the “Mycelioid” particle system algorithm as the basis for monthly exploration and development.  Subtitle “DOS” is a nostalgic nod to the first computer I learned to code on — a 100 MHz 486 CPU beast. The pixelated output resembles high-quality graphics of the time. The palette consists of 16 colors of CGA (including “tweaked brown”). Shuffling the palette order with every seed results in rich, perceivable color variety. Only after this stage, the colors are blended in a modern manner.  “Mycelioid DOS” follows Bitcoin’s advancement. Each block mined not only alters the setup, but begins a celebratory sequence of rapid movement.  The extra feature allows you to input your own seed or blockheight manually: — press [S] on keyboard to open the input window.

It is the 8th in the series, was inscribed on 08.08.2024, and code length is 8,888 bytes. The placement of two main attractors generates an infinity sign inspired path (horizontal 8).  “Mycelioid INF” reacts to Bitcoin’s ongoing development. A temporary spike in particle movement speed signals the new block. The initial setup and behavior of the system is determined by the most recent Bitcoin block hash. With every new block, we experience the new configuration. The algorithm is also reactive to blockchain fees, yet it will unveil its full potential only with extremely high fees.  The extra feature allows you to input your own seed or blockheight manually: — press [S] on keyboard to open the input window.

Inspired by synesthesia, this project explores how the mind interprets form and color when they merge into a dynamic structure.

metadata.Title: Mycelioid LUSH
metadata.Description: “Mycelioid LUSH” is the 9th entry in the art journal on blockchain. I use the “Mycelioid” particle system algorithm as the basis for monthly exploration and development.  “Mycelioid LUSH” encapsulates the essence of 2024 – a year of growth, interconnection, and evolution – while extending a wish for abundance, vitality, and transformation as we step into 2025. This piece invites you to dive into its luminous, organic forms and embark on a journey of introspection.  This piece is not only a celebration of the past year but also a beacon for the future, encouraging growth, resilience, and embracing the ever-changing patterns of our lives. May this artwork inspire a deeper connection to yourself and the world around you, lighting the path to a vibrant and abundant 2025.  “Mycelioid LUSH” responds dynamically to Bitcoin’s ongoing development. Each new block triggers a collision and explosion sequence, marking its arrival. The system’s initial setup and behavior is determined by the most recent Bitcoin block hash, creating a fresh configuration with every block. Additionally, the algorithm adapts based on the number of transactions in the latest block, adding another layer of reactivity.

metadata.Title: Gleam
metadata.Description: Gleam continues my exploration of the generative approaches to light and color, marking a significant turn in my artistic practice. It’s the first artwork where I applied specific algorithms to gain greater control over these elements. While the techniques have evolved since, this piece is where it all began. It’s also where I fully embraced both the limitations and possibilities of a deeper understanding of pure JavaScript coding. Created as a thank-you for early support in the Ordinals space, Gleam is dedicated to the supporters and collectors of my first generative Ordinals project, Rays.

metadata.Title: MemFlux
metadata.Description: MemFlux is a generative exploration of light as the essence of photography. Vibrant lights interact, forming abstract murmuration patterns influenced by deterministic values. Their shifting behaviors reveal structures reminiscent of natural phenomena in constant motion.  Beyond its deterministic output, MemFlux features an interactive mode that fetches live data from a Bitcoin node, dynamically altering the artwork. Mempool transactions affect light movement, blockchain growth influences blur, and difficulty shifts control radii. Total fees regulate speed, resetting in short-term cycles. This continuous data stream makes the artwork unpredictable and ever-evolving.  MemFlux uses the Bitcoin RPC protocol for longevity. If default nodes fail, users can manually input a node address.

metadata.Title: Phantasmagoria
metadata.Description: Phantasmagoria refers to the subject of dreaming and image creation, drawing inspiration from classical painters' mastery of light and the way early video games rendered color and texture. Some outputs evoke the hazy, shape-blending aesthetics of early GAN-generated images - familiar yet unreal.  The algorithm is deeply rooted in digital imaging techniques. The first layer, based on RGB channel mixing, forms an invisible digital universe of orbiting bodies. A second layer distorts it with natural noise, transforming it into something dreamlike - an abstract phantasmagoria.  The result is a semi-pixelated animation with organic motion, shifting between technical precision and natural fluidity.

metadata.Title: Flamelock

metadata.Title: Elapsed
metadata.Description: Elapsed visualizes the blockchain in motion, with swirling particles marking each new Bitcoin block. Two spirits observe - the impatient Mercurial and the introspective Saturnine.  The artwork visualizes the passage of each mined Bitcoin block. Vibrant bits orbit in spirals, knotted loops, or along a shimmering horizon, awaiting the next surge of data. When a new block appears, the scene resets, and the cycle begins again.  Elapsed comes in two distinct variations. FLOAT presents the artwork as originally intended - smooth, fluid, and precise. INT, in contrast, reflects a stage of experimentation, with low-precision movement, glitched positions, and flickering lights. This is the artist’s workshop - a raw sketch before refinement - a hint of analogue nostalgia.

metadata.Title: Astral Arranger
metadata.Artifishal Notes: Constellations are arranged, but never owned. Here, the bouquet is not held—it is exhaled. Each petal, a planet. Each bloom, a star. The arrangement is an accident that pretends to be a pattern.

metadata.Title: RayStone
metadata.Description: A generative tribute to Runestone - a gift to the community. RayStone is a complex generative composition featuring an interactive 3D model of Runestone, hard-coded in just 13.5 kB of JavaScript with a recursive call to P5.js. Enjoy the search for Glyphs, Engravings, Transcendence, and the elusive 1%!

metadata.Title: Stitcher
metadata.Artifishal Notes: A seam that does not mend, but reveals. The edges do not meet—they negotiate. The self is a collage, always unfinished. A hypothesis: To stitch something together is to acknowledge it was never whole.

metadata.Title: Grailstone
metadata.Description: Grailstone is an interactive 3D generative artwork that captures the essence of natural crystals while intertwining with the Bitcoin blockchain. Each piece evolves through 64 unique stages over 8 weeks of human time (8192 blocks), its transformation shaped by real-time blockchain data.  No two Grailstones are alike - transaction patterns, block timestamps, and even the rarity of the inscribed satoshi influence their growth, making each final form truly unpredictable.  Merging nature’s intricacy with digital permanence, Grailstone is both a tribute to the Earth’s hidden sculptures and a testament to the ever-unfolding blockchain.

metadata.Title: Mother of Pangaea
metadata.Artifishal Notes: Before separation, there was one land. Before fragmentation, there was one face. She is the first map, the original whole, the moment before identity becomes plural.

metadata.Title: Spill
metadata.Artifishal Notes: A rupture that does not break, but spills. A single crack is an entire history.

metadata.Title: Spectrum's Edge
metadata.Artifishal Notes: A spectrum is not a color, but an edge—an incision between one state and another. The head does not divide the light; the light divides the head.

metadata.title: Big Tech-bacco
metadata.about: Much like Big Tobacco in the 20th century, modern tech giants flood us with addictive, harmful products, the full consequences of which we are only beginning to understand.  Big Tech presents itself as a pillar of progress—the do-gooders of the future— while disguising the damage under billions in marketing dollars and endless profits, all while eroding our minds and society itself.  "Big Tech-bacco" is an art collection exploring the unsettling parallels between Big Tobacco of the past and Big Tech of today—examining our addiction to screens, social media, one-click consumerism, and beyond.  But the most important question remains: do we have a way out?

metadata.Bio: Ambi aka Irina Koksharova is a multidisciplinary ambidextrous artist and photographer from Ukraine. With the background of artistic work in watercolor and acrylic mediums since 2014, she developed the skill of drawing with both hands in 2020. The collection of ambidextrous continuous line art "Beautiful Bodies" was her first body of work minted on eth in 2021. Due to the war in Ukraine, Irina had to relocate in 2022 and is currently based in Portugal. In her work, Ambi explores different physical and digital creative mediums, often mixing them together to express her ideas.  Artistic name Ambi comes from "ambidextrous" as simultaneous drawing with both hands became Irina's signature style. To achieve more texture and expression, she incorporates physical objects such as gemstones and paper sculpture in her paintings and ambidextrous work.  Combining physical art with photography and digital illustration Ambi takes them to the peak of layering meanings, evokes profound emotional responses and conveys intricate stories.

metadata.Title: Self Portrait by EP
metadata.Info: "This self-portrait represents a turning point in my artistic practice, being my first ever self-portrait. The work stands out for its innovative approach that exploits the principle of recursion as a fundamental compositional method. Through self-assembling elements, the image emerges from an intricate dialogue between colorful geometric shapes and overlapping ordinals, all modulated by a grainy, fabric-like texture that adds tactile depth without altering the original color palette. Recursion is not only a technical expedient, but becomes a metaphor for the process of identity construction: seemingly disconnected fragments that, through repetitive patterns and algorithmic relationships, converge to form a coherent image of the self. This work marks the beginning of an artistic exploration that intertwines personal expression with mathematical and computational principles."

metadata.title: Marcel Schwittlick: Caltech Studies
metadata.about: In the Caltech Studies series, Schwittlick appropriates one of computer vision's foundational moments: the manual annotation of over 9,000 images that formed the first systematic attempt to teach machines to "see." These gestural traces, originally created by three scientists meticulously outlining objects with computer mice, are transformed through various distinct approaches.

metadata.title: Caltech Studies (Braille)
metadata.location: Nguyen Wahed, 504 E 12th St, New York, NY 10009
metadata.about: Using traditional braille printing technology, Schwittlick transforms the scientists' mouse movements into tactile compositions through the mechanical precision of the braille embosser - typically used for transcribing text - which here becomes a tool for rendering digital gestures into a haptic format, creating works that cannot be seen but touched. // Marcel Schwittlick's "White Show" presents a decade-long investigation into the aesthetics of human-machine gesture, manifested through three distinct yet interconnected bodies of work. At its core, the exhibition builds upon historical captures of the cursor – an extension of human gesture into virtual space – as both a personal artistic medium and an artifact of human-machine interaction. Schwittlick's work reveals these daily gestures - our clicks, drags, and hovers - as something far more embodied than mere utility, a choreography of modern existence, each movement a negotiation between flesh and pixel, intention and interface.

metadata.Title: INCISIONS
metadata.Description: This collection is an exact reproduction of the 1981 A.P.I (Artist Proof 1) set of etchings/monotypes by Michael Hafftka.   The set was created in an edition of 26 plus 4 artist’s proof, one bon à tirer and one state proof.   This set, API, is in the British Museum. Set No. 18 is in the collection of the Museum of Modern Art, NY.   Each set contains an etched title page, 10 etchings and an etched colophon page. The physical sets are boxed in a custom binding box designed by the artist.   The artist chose to wipe each plate a little differently which resulted in some variations among the sets.
Polylith exists within a liminal space. Observation and action intertwine, where the future and the past, stillness and motion converge, giving rise to a flow shaped by both change and continuity.

metadata.name: Temporal Echoes
metadata.description: Temporal Echoes dynamically visualizes blockchain activity, transforming a SVG portrait into a pulsing neural network and a fluid background that react to real-time data like transaction volume and fee rates. Through intricate animation and subtle 3D effects, the artwork translates abstract blockchain information into a captivating, living representation of the network's state.
metadata.concept: Temporal Echoes dynamically visualizes blockchain activity, layering a pulsing neural network derived from a portrait with a unique WebGL representation of time. The WebGL shader base layer visualizes time as echoing layers of concentric rings that pulse outward, each representing a 'temporal echo' from a previous state, fading as they expand. Fee rates adjust the ring thickness, while transaction counts affect the background texture, creating a dynamic visualization of the blockchain's ongoing activity. Enhanced by intricate animation and subtle 3D effects, the artwork translates abstract blockchain information into a captivating, living representation of the network's state.
metadata.viewing_instructions: The artwork updates in real-time as new blocks are added to the Bitcoin blockchain. Temporal shift effects occur when new blocks are detected.

metadata.name: Neural Evolution
metadata.description: A dynamic neural network visualization that evolves in response to Bitcoin blockchain data, featuring a portrait foundation with a special 'third eye' founder node that facilitates cross-artwork communication on the same sat.

attributes.description: The neural network consists of up to 100 nodes that form, connect, reproduce, and expire based on genetic traits and blockchain activity.
Neural nodes are organized into 5 distinct families with shared visual and behavioral characteristics.

This fuzzy little gremlin has a white belly with a crescent moon that’s basically a satoshi-sized middle finger to the moon—glowing with the kind of lunar energy that makes miners weep. The brown face? It’s got a smirk that says, ‘I just rug-pulled your entire NFT collection, and I’m here for your tuna.’ Those tiny black eyes are like private keys to a wallet full of mischief, and the tie-dye background—pink, blue, yellow, green—is what happens when you let a cat loose on a testnet with a bucket of paint and a dream. Gizmo’s got a flirty little wink that might make you send some BTC her way, but mostly she’s here to knock over your nodes and nap on your private keys. Meow-nificent chaos, inscribed for eternity!

metadata.Letter to the Church — April 4, 2025: This letter was written two years after the death of my brother, Fr. Melvin Pasco Castro—after two years of silence, denial, and quiet erasure.  It is not a request. It is not a tribute.   It is a record of betrayal, memory, and the decision to reclaim what was taken:   my name, my voice, and my right to exist in the truth.  This inscription marks the beginning of a permanent dual-chain preservation:  📜 Letter recorded on-chain via Bitcoin (Ordinals Protocol)   🎥 Companion video NFT minted on TON Network  Etched eternally. Unaltered. Undeniable.  ✍️ Mildfred P. Castro

metadata.title: Exposed, 2112
metadata.description: In a future where our physical bodies are gone but our data persists, Exposed, 2112 explores identity reconstructed through artificial intelligence. Inspired by the Borg of Star Trek, this work examines the assimilation of human memory into a vast digital collective.  The process began with the most intimate human feature: the eye. Using a Canon 5D MIV and macro lens, I photographed the irises of my family, isolating only the color patterns in Photoshop. These fragments were fused into one composite iris—no longer tied to any single person. I then fed this hybrid into an AI generator, which reimagined the eye within its own visual logic. The AI outputs were layered with human elements—my original irises and holographic images from family ​t​rips—embedded within the pupils.  The result: a gaze that is both human and machine—haunting, fragmented, and shared. It is not simply a portrait of digital assimilation; it is assimilation itself.
